name: hh-meanrev-micro: vol-scaled deep fade, ATR-multiple stop (5m)
rationale: MECHANISM: the SIZE of a reliable snapback scales with realized volatility — the same bb_z=-2 is a much larger dollar dislocation in a high-ATR regime, so the required fade depth and the stop distance must both scale with ATR rather than being a fixed percentage. Momentum-chasers and stop-runs push price to a vol-proportional extreme; the fader collects a spread proportional to the vol they warehouse. This persists because volatility itself mean-reverts (spikes then contracts to baseline), so an ATR-normalized rule auto-adapts: the edge is a fixed number of ATRs from the mean (stationary across regimes), where a fixed-% rule decays. Entry: bb_z at a deep fitted washout confirmed by rsi oversold (a deep dislocation). The STOP is set as atr_mult x ATR at the entry bar (not a fixed %), so risk scales with the regime. Long-only spot; exit on bb_z reversion. DISCONFIRMER: compare the ATR-stop version vs a plain fixed-% stop on the SAME symbols — if ATR-normalization does not reduce the spread of monthly returns, the machinery is noise. Fatal: if it only makes money in the single highest-vol month (one crash bottom), the ATR scaling is masking a tail bet — kill.
catalyst: deep multi-sigma washout with a volatility-scaled (ATR-multiple) stop
